entities.summary:
Domenico Caracciolo, marquess of Villamaina (d. 1789), was a pivotal Neapolitan diplomat and statesman whose career spanned the latter half of the 18th century, a period marked by the Bourbon monarchy's attempts to modernize the Kingdom of Naples through Enlightenment-inspired reforms. Born into a prominent Neapolitan noble family, Caracciolo distinguished himself through a series of significant diplomatic postings in London and Paris before undertaking his most challenging assignment as Viceroy of Sicily, where he confronted the deeply entrenched power of the island's feudal aristocracy. His work was central to the broader European struggle between absolutist monarchies seeking to centralize power and traditional feudal structures resisting change.

Caracciolo's diplomatic career included serving as ambassador to Great Britain from 1764 to 1771, where he observed the workings of a constitutional monarchy, and subsequently as ambassador to France from 1771 to 1781. In Paris, he immersed himself in the intellectual ferment of the Enlightenment, forging connections with prominent philosophes like Jean le Rond d'Alembert and Denis Diderot, whose ideas profoundly shaped his reformist zeal. Upon his return to Naples, Ferdinand IV appointed him Viceroy of Sicily in 1781, a role in which he vigorously pursued the abolition of torture, the reduction of feudal privileges, and a cadastral survey to rationalize land ownership and taxation. He also served briefly as President of the Supreme Council of Finance and Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Royal Household in Naples from 1786 until his death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Domenico Caracciolo's tenure as Viceroy of Sicily directly challenged the deeply entrenched feudal system and introduced significant Enlightenment-inspired reforms, impacting the administrative and social structures of the Kingdom of Naples. His efforts, though met with resistance, laid groundwork for future modernization attempts and highlighted the persistent struggle against aristocratic power in 18th-century Italy.
